chunks: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them, the Almighty, the All-Forgiving.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Allah being the Lord of the heavens and the earth?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Sad, this verse serves as a rhetorical climax to the narrative of Prophet Solomon, affirming Allah's absolute sovereignty over the cosmos while balancing His majesty with mercy. Shia exegetes often highlight the juxtaposition of Al-Aziz (the Mighty) and Al-Ghaffar (the Forgiving) to illustrate that divine power is the foundation for divine grace, encouraging believers to seek forgiveness through recognition of God's ultimate authority.
